chapters.title: THE MAGNITUDE OF THE STARS
chapters.exactFinalPrompt:
Use case: historical-scene
Asset type: full-resolution chapter illustration for a deluxe illustrated edition of Pliny the Elder, Natural History, Book II, chapter 11
Primary request: Interpret Pliny's reasoning about the immense magnitude of the Sun, Moon, and Earth through the silent evidence of nature. Show a vast plain at equinox with several long, perfectly parallel rows of mature trees receding for miles; every tree casts a long shadow at the same angle toward the viewer. Beyond them, Mount Ida rises fully within the distant horizon while an enormous plain Sun disk rises behind it, visibly broader than the whole mountain and extending far to both sides without touching the canvas edge. Tiny fully visible Roman surveyors stand among the rows, comparing the parallel shadows with simple cords and staffs, made humble by the scale of the Sun.
Scene/backdrop: broad ancient Mediterranean plain at dawn, Mount Ida in the distance, no city or modern structure
Style/medium: original Plinian natural-history folio illustration on warm aged vellum; iron-gall linework; fine cross-hatching and stipple; restrained hand-applied mineral pigments; ancient, timeless, beautiful, rough and polished at once; coherent with a deluxe Roman natural-history codex

chapters.exactFinalPrompt:

Asset type: full-resolution chapter illustration for a deluxe illustrated edition of Pliny the Elder, Natural History, Book II, chapter 13
Primary request: Interpret Pliny's account of the recurrence of solar and lunar eclipses and why the same eclipse is visible in some lands but hidden in others. chapters.title: MOTION OF THE MOON
chapters.exactFinalPrompt:
Use case: historical-scene
Asset type: full-resolution chapter illustration for a deluxe illustrated edition of Pliny the Elder, Natural History, Book II, chapter 14
Primary request: Interpret Pliny's observations on the Moon's daily motion, its waxing and waning horns turned away from the Sun, and the stars that remain present in daylight though ordinarily hidden. Make a dramatic single scene organized around a complete ancient circular stone well in the lower center: one Roman observer stands fully visible on steps within the dark shaft, looking upward, and several faint stars become visible in the deep blue patch of sky seen through the well's shadowed mouth. Far above and beyond the well, a bright plain Sun disk hangs to one side while a graceful arc of successive Moon positions crosses the open sky—from a slender waxing crescent whose horns turn away from the Sun, through a full Moon at the farthest point, to a slender waning crescent whose horns again turn away from the Sun. A second small observer beside the well compares the sky from daylight to depth.
Scene/backdrop: quiet ancient Mediterranean terrace with low hills and sparse olive trees beneath an immense daytime sky; the stone well is unadorned and functional; no city or monumental architecture
Style/medium: original Plinian natural-history folio illustration on warm aged vellum; iron-gall linework; fine cross-hatching and stipple; restrained hand-applied mineral pigments; ancient, timeless, beautiful, rough and polished at once; coherent with a deluxe Roman natural-history codex
Composition/framing: landscape 3:2 with unusual vertical depth; the complete circular well and both fully visible observers anchor the lower center, its dark shaft opening into a small lapis pool with visible stars; the fully contained Sun and all successive lunar disks float high above on one spacious implied arc; one complete unified scene; generous negative space and breathing room around every celestial body, person, tree, and the entire well rim; no primary subject touches or crosses an edge

Constraints: the well must have a complete unbroken circular rim with no inscription; the celestial bodies are plain natural disks without faces; Moon positions are clearly successive moments along one implied motion, not a decorative border; crescent horns must point away from the Sun; historically plausible Roman dress; no scrolls, tablets, dials, clocks, or instruments; one independent full scene, not an atlas, panel grid, contact sheet, collage, cutaway diagram, chart, or crop
Avoid: all lettering, captions, labels, numerals, pseudo-writing, inscriptions, signatures, logos, watermarks, arrows, arrowheads, orbit lines, tick marks, zodiac symbols, modern notation, telescopes, modern objects, photography, photorealism, glossy digital rendering, neon color, magical beams, cropped well, cropped rim, cropped people, cropped Sun, cropped Moon disks, multiple panels
